ai.title: web-scraper switches to jina.ai proxy
ai.summary: npm-app/src/web-scraper.ts now fetches `https://r.jina.ai/${url}` via axios instead of the target URL directly. Local cheerio parsing and `$('body').text()` extraction are commented out; proxy response body is stored raw in `scrapedPagesCache`. Affects the web scraping subsystem only.

eli5.text: The web scraper now uses a different method to read web pages. Instead of fetching a website's content directly and then cleaning it up with local parsing tools, it now retrieves pre-processed text through a third-party proxy service that returns the content in a clean, ready-to-use format. The raw text it returns is stored directly in the cache without any local processing being applied. This change is live today and affects only the internal web scraping functionality, with no visible impact to end users.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.117
ai.summary: Bump `npm-app/package.json` version to 1.0.117. Internal release metadata update. No functional changes.

eli5.text: Your AI assistant received a routine update that keeps everything working smoothly behind the scenes. Two smaller improvements are now available: the assistant skips running certain setup commands that don't need to be run again, and it can now pull information from web pages more reliably using a new method. If you use the assistant today, these changes are already active. If you're checking your installed version, you'd see the numbers in its settings have advanced, but that alone doesn't mean anything new is visibly different.
